newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine broadens foreign access to T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine broadens foreign access to T-bills.

text.p: Ukraine, keen to attract foreign investment, is making it easier for foreigners to buy its Treasury bills, the head of the central bank said.

"In our resolution, which will be published in the near future, buyers from any foreign country can buy T-bills on the primary and secondary markets, through Ukrainian banks," National Bank of Ukraine chairman Viktor Yushchenko told a news conference late on Wednesday.
Yushchenko said many potential buyers had been deterred because until now only licensed commercial banks have been allowed to buy, hold and sell bills on behalf of clients.
"We want to significantly widen our securities market in 1997," he said.
Foreigners would be able to open accounts in local currency for trading securities at licensed banks, he said. Currently 58 banks have the appropriate licence.
The liberalisation follows similar moves in Russia.
The issue of whether a 30 percent capital gains tax and profit tax applies to T-bill buyers has not yet been settled.
Sources in the Tax Inspection Department said documents clearing up the taxation issue would be ready by the end of this week.
Ukraine has never forbidden foreigners from buying its government securities, but uncertainty about tax has put off most potential investors.
At the last auction of three- and six-month paper on August 28, the average yield was 57.30 and 59.90 percent respectively. The finance ministry also issues nine- and 12-month paper.
Central bank officials have previously said foreign buying would be limited to 35 percent.
The central bank plans to raise $852 million in T-bill sales in 1996 to cover the projected $2.6 billion deficit.
Yushchenko said that by next year Ukraine should not have to cover its deficit by printing money, which in the past has fuelled inflation and devalued the old karbovanets currency.
The karbovanets is being taken out of circulation by September 16, after the introduction of the new hryvnya currency on September 2.
"In 1997 the budget should have two sources to cover its deficit - the domestic and foreign securities markets," he said.
This week Yushchenko said Ukraine intended to issue foreign currency denominated bonds on foreign markets next year. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
